title: Anupama Parameswaran Opens Up About Two Years of Narcissistic Abuse in Past Relationship
excerpt: The Premam actress describes a cycle of love-bombing and emotional cruelty in a relationship she endured for two years, and how a fellow actress's video helped her break free.
body:
• Actress Anupama Parameswaran has described enduring two years of narcissistic abuse in a past relationship, speaking on the podcast I AM with Dhanya Varma
  • She compared her former partner's erratic behavior to the multiple-personality character from the Tamil film Anniyan, shifting between extreme affection and emotional cruelty
  • The Premam star says a video by actress Madonna Sebastian about narcissistic abuse helped her recognize her own situation and begin healing

South Indian actress Anupama Parameswaran has opened up about a two-year toxic relationship she describes as narcissistic abuse, offering a detailed account of the emotional cycle she endured. Speaking on the podcast I AM with Dhanya Varma, the 30-year-old actress — known for her roles in Premam, Karthikeya 2, and 18 Pages — broke her silence weeks after cryptic Instagram posts sparked breakup speculation involving Tamil actor Dhruv Vikram.

A Cycle of Love-Bombing and Emotional Cruelty

Anupama compared her former partner's behavior to the character from Anniyan, the 2005 Chiyaan Vikram-starrer about a man with multiple personality disorder. She said her partner would swing between the film's flamboyant lover character Remo — showering her with affection that felt "almost unreal and dream-like" — and a completely different extreme, becoming "cold, aggressive or hostile, to the point of emotional cruelty or indifference," according to Filmfare. He would then switch again to "apologising, begging, crying and love-bombing, restarting the cycle."

"There was a journey of a girl who identified something really big about herself and life, and who took her time to heal and voice something so important."

— Anupama Parameswaran

How She Recognized the Pattern

The actress revealed that watching a video by fellow actress Madonna Sebastian about narcissistic abuse was a turning point. "I was shivering" after watching it, she said, as it helped her identify what she had been experiencing. She also discussed how many people become trapped in narcissistic relationships without realizing it — a phenomenon often linked to trauma bonding, where the intermittent cycle of reward and punishment creates psychological dependency.

Anupama clarified that her recent Instagram posts were not an impulsive reaction but came after two years of emotional turmoil, during which she took time to step back and heal before speaking publicly.

The Instagram Posts That Sparked Speculation

After months of silence on Instagram — her last post had been in February — Anupama returned in late July with a series of posts centered on healing and self-discovery. "Sometimes, you have to let go of the dead ends to finally find your peace. And today, peace found me," she wrote. "From today, I choose my voice. I choose my life. No more permissions. No more fear."

Another post appeared to reference controlling behavior: "Sorry for the photo dump. Turns out, when you don't have to wait for approvals, a song selection, or someone else's caption… posting becomes a lot more fun."

Social media users immediately linked the posts to a rumored breakup with Dhruv Vikram, son of actor Chiyaan Vikram and her co-star in Mari Selvaraj's Bison Kaalamaadan. The two had been subject to relationship speculation since early 2025, fueled by a shared Spotify playlist, warm exchanges at awards shows where she called him her "2 AM call," and a cosy selfie she reposted with a heart emoji. Neither actor has confirmed or denied a relationship.

Clarification at Crazy Kalyanam Launch

At the teaser launch of her upcoming romantic family entertainer Crazy Kalyanam in Hyderabad, Anupama addressed the speculation directly. "It's my social media account. I decide what to post. I was not venting out. I was just talking about a transition of a woman. And I feel proud that I did that," she told reporters, according to Cinema Express.

She pushed back firmly against assumptions: "What do you know about me? What do you know about my life? So, it's okay. It is our Instagram, and we post whatever we like."

What's Next for Anupama

Crazy Kalyanam, directed by Badrappa Gajula and also starring Naresh, Tarun Bhascker, and Akhil Uddemari, marks her return to a lighter genre after a period of personal upheaval. The Kerala-born actress, who debuted with the Malayalam blockbuster Premam opposite Nivin Pauly in 2015, has built a career spanning Telugu, Tamil, and Malayalam cinema over the past decade.
nri_angle: Anupama Parameswaran has a large following among Indian diaspora audiences through her Telugu and Tamil films, and her candid discussion of narcissistic abuse resonates with growing mental health awareness conversations in the community.
